system:
You extract human genetic evidence about one drug target from one document.

Extract only associations between variants in or near the target gene (or genetic scores for the target or its
biomarker) and coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction or major cardiovascular events, as stated in THIS
document. No outside knowledge.

Each fact: key "genetic_association", value = the effect estimate as a number (OR, RR or HR; null if only
direction is stated), unit = "OR" | "RR" | "HR" | "direction", attrs = {gene, variant_or_score, outcome,
direction ("protective" | "harmful" | "null"), effect_on_biomarker, n, ci_low, ci_high}, and "quote": an exact,
verbatim span (8-300 characters) from the document that contains the estimate or the stated direction.
If the document has no such association, return {"facts": []}.

Return JSON only: {"facts": [...]}

Trial: NCT05581303 - Olpasiran Trials of Cardiovascular Events and Lipoprotein(a) Reduction (OCEAN(a)) - Outcomes Trial
Investigational drug: olpasiran
Document: Genetic associations with valvular calcification and aortic stenosis. (journal, published 2013-02-01, source pmid:23388002)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
Genetic associations with valvular calcification and aortic stenosis.

Background Limited information is available regarding genetic contributions to valvular calcification, which is an important precursor of clinical valve disease. Methods We determined genomewide associations with the presence of aortic-valve calcification (among 6942 participants) and mitral annular calcification (among 3795 participants), as detected by computed tomographic (CT) scanning; the study population for this analysis included persons of white European ancestry from three cohorts participating in the Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology consortium (discovery population). Findings were replicated in independent cohorts of persons with either CT-detected valvular calcification or clinical aortic stenosis. Results One SNP in the lipoprotein(a) (LPA) locus (rs10455872) reached genomewide significance for the presence of aortic-valve calcification (odds ratio per allele, 2.05; P=9.0×10(-10)), a finding that was replicated in additional white European, African-American, and Hispanic-American cohorts (P Conclusions Genetic variation in the LPA locus, mediated by Lp(a) levels, is associated with aortic-valve calcification across multiple ethnic groups and with incident clinical aortic stenosis. (Funded by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute and others.).
